newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MOZAMBIQUE DENIES SUBMARINE DEAL WITH IRAN.
newsitem.headline: MOZAMBIQUE DENIES SUBMARINE DEAL WITH IRAN.

text.p: Mozambique denied reports on Tuesday that it had negotiated a defence agreement with Teheran to harbour Iranian submarines in one or more of its ports.
"Mozambique is not talking to Iran and has not negotiated anything like that," Antonio Matonse, spokesman for the office of Mozambique's President Joaquim Chissano, told Reuters.
Matonse said a rumour about such a deal, which has been reported recently in South African newspapers, had originated in newspapers in Italy.
"It is just a rumour. We have never spoken to the Iranians about that," Matonse said.
Newspaper reports in South Africa say Mozambique has agreed to allow Iran to use its Indian Ocean ports, probably for its three Kilo-class submarines bought from Russia from 1993.
The southern Africa correspondent for Jane's Defence Weekly, Helmoed-Romer Heitman, stated in an article in Business Day newspaper on Tuesday that the accord was a fact.

He said the submarines represented Iran's only real capability to threaten targets outside the Gulf, and would be a priority target in any future Gulf conflict. This explained Tehran's desire to find a safe haven well away from the region.

But, Romer said, by the same token this meant that any future conflict could be "exported" to the Mozambique Channel, with serious implications for Mozambique and its southern Indian Ocean neighbours.
South Africa, worried about the reports, said it had sought clarification from Maputo and had been told that no such agreement had been made.
"We inquired about such a deal and were assured (by the Mozambican government) that none existed," South African deputy foreign minister Aziz Pahad told Reuters.
